clearing_status.fact: On Feb 25 2025, the SEC formally extended compliance dates by one year to Dec 31 2026 (cash) and Jun 30 2027 (repo) via Exchange Act Release No. 34-102487 -- this is already the FIRST official extension. As of Apr 17 2026, SIFMA and IIB exemptive-relief requests remain pending before the SEC (TBAC Charge 1Q2 2026, published May 2026; SEC Commissioner Uyeda statement Apr 20 2026 at sec.gov). No second full deadline extension has been announced as of today.
clearing_status.rationale: The rubric scores 1 when 'an official extension [has been] granted, OR exemptive-relief requests [are] pending.' Both conditions are satisfied: the SEC granted one formal 12-month extension (Feb 2025) and multiple exemptive-relief requests (SIFMA inter-affiliate, IIB extraterritorial) were still pending with open comment periods as of April-May 2026. No second extension order has been found, so the score does not reach 2.

plan_financing.fact: Japan 10-year JGB yield reached 2.901% on ~July 10 2026 (a 30-year high), up from ~2.1% in March — a >70bps rise explicitly attributed to fiscal concerns over PM Takaichi's spending plans and supplementary budget financing ambiguity; yield held at ~2.80% on July 31 2026 (TradingEconomics, CNBC July 14 2026). No auction failure (April 20y BtC 4.82), but the >50bps spike on fiscal concern meets the rubric's Level 2 standalone threshold.
plan_financing.rationale: The >70bps cumulative rise in 10y JGB yield to a 30-year high, driven by Takaichi fiscal expansion concerns and unresolved supplementary budget financing, clears the rubric's '>50bps yield spike on fiscal concern' Level 2 trigger. Auctions are still clearing (no BtC <2 or failed sale), preventing a higher-confidence Level 2 classification, but the yield spike criterion alone is sufficient per the rubric.

dissent.view: Oxford Economics notes 10y yield retreated slightly after June supplementary budget was smaller than feared, and recent auctions remain well-covered; fiscal stress may be elevated but not disorderly

direct_lending_default.fact: Fitch Ratings reported the U.S. private credit default rate (trailing 12-month, inclusive of distressed exchanges and maturity extensions) remained at a record high of 6.0% for Q2 2026 / May 2026, up from 5.7% in Q1, per Investment Executive (July 30 2026) citing Fitch and LSTA Fitch commentary page (June 15 2026): 'Private Credit Default Rate Remains at Record High 6.0% in May 2026'.
direct_lending_default.rationale: The Fitch inclusive measure (counting distressed exchanges, maturity extensions, PIK deferrals) printed 6.0% on a trailing-12-month basis for both April and May 2026 and held through Q2 2026 per Fitch's own quarterly tally of 32 default events involving 20 new defaulters; this anchors the rubric value at 6.0. A LinkedIn Fitch post titled 'U.S. Private Credit Default Rate drops to 5.2% in July' is noted but unverified as of this run and is held in dissent pending a confirmed Fitch publication.

dissent.view: Proskauer Private Credit Default Index (count-based, 697 loans, $189.2B): 2.73% in Q1 2026, up from 1.84% two quarters prior — materially lower because it excludes distressed-exchange-as-default classification and uses count not dollar-weighted TTM
Moody's: distressed restructurings accounted for ~65% of all 2025 private credit defaults; excluding them produces headline rates of 1.6%–4.7%
Fitch LinkedIn post (unverified full text) titled 'U.S. Private Credit Default Rate drops to 5.2% in July' — may represent a July 2026 monthly print; not yet corroborated by a full Fitch publication
BofA (Dec 2025 forecast): expected default rate to ease to 4.5% in 2026 from 5% in 2025 as Fed cuts rates

redemption_gates.fact: In Q1 2026, investors sought to pull >$20.8bn from the largest semi-liquid private credit funds; named funds that triggered their 5% quarterly repurchase caps include BlackRock HLEND (~$26bn, 9.3% requested/5% paid), Cliffwater Corporate Lending Fund (~$33bn, 14-17% requested/5-7% paid), Blackstone BCRED (~$82bn, 7.9% requested, cap raised to 7% in Q1 then held at 5% in Q2 vs. 10% requests), Apollo Debt Solutions BDC (16.8% requested/5% honored), Morgan Stanley North Haven (10.9% requested/5% paid), Golub Capital (8.5% requested/~59% pro-rated in Q2), and Blue Owl OBDC II (permanently halted redemptions Feb. 19, 2026) plus OCIC and OTIC (capped at 5% against $5.4bn in requests by Apr. 2, 2026). Source: CRS IN12674 (Mar. 27, 2026), Bloomberg (Apr. 2, 2026), SEC filings, Cobalt Intelligence analysis (Apr. 22, 2026), Yahoo Finance/Investing.com (Jun. 4, 2026).
redemption_gates.rationale: At least 8 named private-credit/BDC funds with aggregate AUM far exceeding $100bn triggered redemption gates or quarterly repurchase caps within the same Q1 2026 window, with Blue Owl OBDC II imposing a permanent halt. This vastly satisfies the WIDESPREAD threshold of >=3 largest funds or combined AUM >$100bn gating in the same quarter.

new_imf_programs.fact: In the trailing 6 months (Feb–Aug 2026), at least 3 sovereigns received newly approved IMF arrangements: (1) Ukraine — new 48-month EFF of US$8.1bn approved 26 Feb 2026 (imf.org/en/news/articles/2026/02/26/pr-26066-ukraine); (2) Mauritania — new 42-month ECF/EFF approved 24 Jun 2026 (imf.org/en/news/articles/2026/06/24/pr26223-mauritania); (3) Burkina Faso — new RSF arrangement approved 18 Feb 2026 (imf.org/en/news/articles/2026/05/26/pr26170-burkina-faso). No new EM missed coupons or fresh sovereign defaults were identified in the window.
new_imf_programs.rationale: Three sovereigns received newly approved IMF arrangements within the 6-month window, meeting the rubric's CLUSTER threshold of >=3 sovereigns newly in IMF programs. No missed coupon events were identified, so the stress is concentrated in program entries rather than outright default.

dissent.view: Burkina Faso RSF may be classified as a climate/resilience facility rather than a distress-driven bailout arrangement, which could reduce the count to 2 (Ukraine + Mauritania), implying RISING (value=1) rather than CLUSTER.

china_ppi.fact: NBS official release dated 2026-07-10 states: 'In June 2026, China's producer price index for industrial products (PPI) increased by 4.1% year on year' — source: https://www.stats.gov.cn/english/PressRelease/202607/t20260710_1964093.html
china_ppi.rationale: The rubric requires the signed NBS figure for the latest published month; +4.1% YoY for June 2026 is directly from the NBS English-language press release. The engine scores on size of move: +4.1% represents a notable positive cost-push signal, exporting input-cost pressure globally.

trade_actions.fact: In the trailing 3 months (May–Aug 2026), at least 5 distinct major-economy measures were imposed: (1) USTR new 12.5% Section 301 tariff on China for forced-labor failures, effective 24 Jul 2026 (china-briefing.com, 23 Jul 2026); (2) USTR broad Section 301 round hitting ~60 countries incl. China with 10-12.5% tariffs, announced 23 Jul 2026 (avalara.com, rte.ie); (3) China MOFCOM export-control ban on 10 US rare-earth/critical-mineral entities, 22 Jun 2026 (washingtonpost.com, morganlewis.com); (4) China MOFCOM export-control ban on 14 EU dual-use entities incl. Rheinmetall, ~Jul 7-24 2026 (legalinsurrection.com, tech-insider.org); (5) China MOFCOM Announcement No. 26 of 2026 formalizing strategic-mineral export-control enforcement mechanism, Jun 2026 (morganlewis.com).
trade_actions.rationale: Five or more distinct new major-economy trade measures are confirmed within the trailing 3-month window, clearly exceeding the rubric threshold of >=4 measures for ESCALATING (score 2); China's two targeted export-ban rounds against US and EU entities constitute explicit tit-for-tat escalation steps beyond a managed truce, and the IEA flagged $6.5T downstream exposure as a volume/price corroborant of real disruption.

dissent.view: The Nov 2025 US-China truce (rare-earth suspension to Nov 2026) is still nominally in force for the suspended Oct 2025 measures, suggesting a partial managed-truce framework persists even as new entity-level controls are added; some analysts may characterize the targeted entity bans as sub-threshold enforcement rather than broad escalation.

license_flow.fact: MOFCOM April 2025 Announcement No. 18 case-by-case licensing for 7 heavy/medium REEs and magnet products remains fully active and unsuspended; general licences issued Dec 2025 to only ~3 named magnet makers (JL MAG, San Huan, Yunsheng) and are not broadly available; actual approval times run 60-120+ days against a 45-working-day statutory target; on 22 June 2026 MOFCOM added 10 US entities (incl. MP Materials, USA Rare Earth) to the export control list with immediate categorical denial; on 24 July 2026 MOFCOM Announcement No. 30 placed 14 EU entities incl. Rheinmetall on the Export Control Watchlist; Reuters reported 20 July 2026 that Japan received zero shipments of dysprosium, terbium, or yttrium in June 2026; NdPr alloy benchmark rose ~21.4% in one month through 1 July 2026. Sources: tech-insider.org (2026-07-30), mainrichinternational.com (Jul 2026), news.metal.com (2026-07-29), morganlewis.com (2026-07-01), techtimes.com (2026-05-27).
license_flow.rationale: The regime is case-by-case with general licences available only to a whitelist of ~3 named producers, processing times materially exceed 30 days (60-120+ days in practice), and new entity-level categorical denials were added within the trailing 3 months (US entity list June 22, EU watchlist July 24) — all squarely fitting rubric level 1 (SLOWING). Level 2 is not assigned globally because civilian commercial approvals continue to flow for non-listed buyers, but the Japan zero-shipment volume signal and entity-list categorical denials represent a credible dissent toward 2.

truce_status.fact: The Nov-10 2025 truce (MOFCOM suspension of Oct-9 2025 rare-earth controls) remains formally in force until Nov 10 2026, confirmed by a senior US official on ~May 11 2026 ('It\'s still in effect, it doesn\'t expire yet' - E&E News/Reuters, May 12 2026). However, on June 22 2026 China\'s MOFCOM added 10 US entities - including rare-earth miners MP Materials and USA Rare Earth - to its export control list, a targeted but real entity-list addition that analysts at SCMP (June 23 2026) called 'one of the most significant escalations since the Busan truce.' The truce suspension itself expires Nov 10 2026, placing it within the rubric\'s <90-day window as of ~Aug 12 2026.
truce_status.rationale: The truce has not lapsed (ruling out score 2), but two rubric triggers for score 1 are met: (a) the nominal expiry of Nov 10 2026 is now fewer than 100 days away with no confirmed renewal, and (b) the June 22 2026 entity-list additions of MP Materials and USA Rare Earth constitute a partial breach of the truce\'s spirit, even though they are entity-specific rather than a blanket reimposition of controls.

re_blacklist.fact: China MOFCOM Announcement No. 23 of 2026 (issued 22 June 2026) added 10 named US entities to its export-control list under the Export Control Law and Dual-Use Items Regulations, including specifically MP Materials Corp and USA Rare Earth; the full list per Global Times/MOFCOM: Aveox, Red Cat Holdings, Teal Drones, IMSAR, Jaia Robotics, Ball Aerospace & Technologies Corp, Oshkosh Defense, L3Harris Maritime Services, MP Materials Corp, and USA Rare Earth. Multiple corroborating sources (Benchmark Minerals, Al Jazeera, Bloomberg, Taipei Times, Global Times) confirm the measure is entity-specific, not a categorical sector-wide ban. Share-price reaction was muted: MP Materials roughly flat, USA Rare Earth modestly higher on announcement day (Reuters via StockTitan).
re_blacklist.rationale: Two named US rare-earth producers (MP Materials, USA Rare Earth) are explicitly listed by MOFCOM as of 22 June 2026, satisfying rubric level 1 (entity-specific). Multiple authoritative sources and the muted market signal both confirm this is a firm-specific action, not a sector-wide categorical ban (level 2).

hree_premium.fact: Ucore Rare Metals (Feb 23 2026, Newsfile/Barchart): dysprosium oxide >$200/kg China vs ~$1,000/kg ex-China (~5x); terbium $900/kg China vs >$4,500/kg ex-China (~5x). Corroborated by Rare Earth Exchanges (June 5 2026): terbium $4,500-$4,700/kg ex-China vs ~$914-$923/kg domestic China (~5x). Benchmark Minerals (March 24 2026) pegged 2025 dysprosium CIF N.America at 4.4x EXW China, forecasting 8.3x by 2027.
hree_premium.rationale: Multiple independent price observations from Feb-June 2026 consistently show ex-China HREE spot prices at approximately 5x Chinese domestic benchmarks for both dysprosium and terbium, driven by China's April 2025 export licensing controls; Benchmark's trajectory (4.4x in 2025 rising to 8.3x by 2027) places mid-2026 squarely near 5-6x, supporting a 5.0 central estimate.

dissent.view: Benchmark Minerals (March 2026) implies current 2026 multiple closer to 6x given linear interpolation between 4.4x (2025) and 8.3x (2027)

Ucore (Feb 23 2026) cited terbium at >$4,500/kg ex-China vs $900/kg China = ~5x, but by July 2026 domestic China terbium had risen to ~$1,292/kg (Rare Earth Exchanges forum), compressing the multiple if ex-China prices did not rise proportionally

genius_impl.fact: The statutory July 18, 2026 deadline for final GENIUS Act implementing rules passed without any agency (OCC, FDIC, Federal Reserve, NCUA, Treasury/FinCEN/OFAC) issuing final regulations; all 10 rule packages remained in proposed/NPRM form, with multiple comment periods running past the deadline (e.g., the five-agency CIP NPRM comment window closes August 21, 2026). Source: cryptobriefing.com, coinpaprika.com, crowdfundinsider.com, cryptodaily.co.uk, all dated ~July 18-20, 2026; corroborated by FDIC.gov, OCC.gov, and federalregister.gov primary filings.
genius_impl.rationale: The rubric scores 2 = PROBLEMS when the deadline is missed without final rules. The July 18, 2026 deadline passed with zero final rules issued across all mandated agencies — a clean deadline miss. No court stay or compliance-failure event is documented, but the plain deadline miss without final rules is sufficient for a score of 2 per rubric.

dissent.view: Some analysts note the missed deadline carries no legal penalty, the GENIUS Act remains in force, and the effective date of January 18, 2027 is unchanged — characterising the situation as a compliance gap rather than a breakdown of the regulatory framework.

ai_revenue_gap.fact: Alphabet Q2 2026 (reported July 22, 2026): capex $44.9B, +100% YoY; Google Cloud revenue $24.8B, +82% YoY; Alphabet RAISED full-year 2026 capex guidance to $195-205B (from $180-190B); free cash flow turned negative (-$5.9B). Microsoft FY Q3 2026: capex $30.88B +84% YoY vs. AI revenue run-rate $37B annualized +123% YoY. Sources: Alphabet 8-K/earnings call July 22 2026 (abc.xyz/investor); CNBC July 22 2026; Yahoo Finance/InsiderFinance.
ai_revenue_gap.rationale: Across the hyperscaler complex, capex growth (Alphabet +100% YoY, Microsoft +84% YoY) exceeds AI-attributable revenue growth (Google Cloud +82% YoY) in the most recent quarter, placing this squarely in the WIDE band (score=1). However, Google Cloud revenue is still strongly accelerating YoY (82%, up from ~55-65% prior quarters) and Microsoft AI revenue (+123% YoY) actually outpaces its capex growth, so there is no AI-revenue QoQ deceleration sufficient to trigger score=2 despite Alphabet raising capex guidance again.

dissent.view: Microsoft AI revenue (+123% YoY, $37B run rate) grew faster than its capex (+84% YoY), suggesting a CLOSING gap (score=0) for MSFT in isolation
Alphabet raising capex to $195-205B while FCF turned negative (-$5.9B) and stock fell 7% could be read as WIDENING FAST (score=2) for Alphabet specifically

gpu_refi_stress.fact: CoreWeave's 5-year CDS spread topped ~855 bps on July 29 2026 (Bloomberg, July 29 2026), implying ~50% cumulative default probability; the company simultaneously was forced to widen pricing on its $2.6B leveraged loan by up to 125 bps and offer it at 97 cents on the dollar before investors would commit, with maintenance covenants added (Bloomberg/Yahoo Finance, July 29 2026). No outright default or distressed exchange has been confirmed as of 2026-08-03.
gpu_refi_stress.rationale: CoreWeave is a named borrower facing a concrete refinancing wall: it had to reprice and restructure a $2.6B facility at a discount and accept tighter covenants, satisfying the Rubric 1 criterion of a named borrower facing a refinancing wall. No confirmed default, distressed exchange, or failed refinancing exists yet to warrant Rubric 2.

dissent.view: Some secondary sources characterize the 855 bps CDS level and 50% default odds as approaching distressed-exchange territory, suggesting Rubric 2 could apply imminently; however no actual default event has been confirmed.

govt_stability.fact: On 2 Feb 2026, France adopted its 2026 budget after two no-confidence motions (LFI: 260 votes, RN: 135 votes) fell short of the 289-vote threshold; PM Lecornu's 'weak minority government' survived, heralding 'a period of relative stability' — Reuters/Al Jazeera, 2 Feb 2026. The National Assembly remains a three-bloc hung parliament with no working majority for any party since the 2024 snap election.
govt_stability.rationale: Lecornu governs a minority government relying on Socialist and Republican abstention to defeat no-confidence motions — no working majority exists, precisely matching rubric band 1 (fragile: minority/hung parliament surviving no-confidence votes but governing). No government collapse or dissolution has occurred since February 2026.

rating_action.fact: S&P downgraded France from AA-/A-1+ to A+/A-1 (spglobal.com, Oct 17 2025); Fitch downgraded France from AA- to A+ with stable outlook (Sep 12-15 2025, per tradingeconomics.com/fxstreet.com); Moody's downgraded France from Aa2 to Aa3 in December 2024 (marketscreener.com) and additionally moved its Aa3 outlook to negative on Oct 24-25 2025 (France24). Moody's additionally carries a negative outlook, but the rating cut itself is dispositive.

dollar_reserve_share.fact: IMF COFER Data Brief (data.imf.org, published July 1 2026): 'The share of US dollar holdings in foreign exchange reserves increased to 57.13 percent in 2026Q1, from 56.42 percent in 2025Q4.'
dollar_reserve_share.rationale: The IMF COFER release dated July 1 2026 is the primary, official source for this indicator; the rubric asks for the latest USD share of allocated global FX reserves as a percent, and 57.13 is that exact figure for the most recent published quarter (2026Q1). No material conflicting official reading exists for this same quarter.

weaponization_event.fact: BRICS Pay began operational deployment in 2026 targeting the New Delhi summit, and the BRICS Unit (40% gold-backed settlement token) completed a pilot launch in Oct 2025 with cross-border trade mechanisms active in 2026; no new sovereign reserve freeze or outright confiscation of Russian or any other state's assets has been executed in 2026 - G7/EU debate on permanent seizure of ~$300bn Russian reserves remains unresolved with CFR (Nov 2025) and IAI (Apr 2026) both confirming all serious options avoid outright confiscation. insurer_exits.fact: Climate Cosmos (June 18, 2026) identifies 13 states with active insurer non-renewal waves in 2026 (CA, FL, TX, GA, OK, CO, LA and others); FL non-renewed 3.35% of policies in 2024 (1.7x 2018 rate) and CA 3.18% (3.9x 2018 rate) per leadgen-economy.com (June 25, 2026); Florida Citizens fell from 1.42M policies (Oct 2023) to ~385-395K by Jan 2026 indicating partial FL market stabilization. insurer_exits.rationale: Thirteen states with documented non-renewal waves sits squarely in the 5-15 state band of the RISING tier; no top-10 insurer is confirmed as fully exiting a major state in 2026, and Florida shows measurable stabilization, precluding the ACCELERATING (2) classification.

dissent.view: The Queen Zone (June 25, 2026) characterizes non-renewals as concentrated in only ~6 states, which would still qualify as RISING but at the lower end of the band.

cat_losses.fact: Global insured nat-cat losses in H1 2026 totalled $44bn (Munich Re, July 30 2026), vs the 10-year H1 average of $50bn — 12% below average; Gallagher Re reports $46bn, 28% below its $64bn decadal average; Aon reports $47bn. Source: https://www.munichre.com/en/company/media-relations/media-information-and-corporate-news/media-information/2026/natural-disaster-figures-first-half-2026.html
cat_losses.rationale: YTD insured losses of $44-47bn sit at or below the 10-year average of $50-64bn (well under 150% of average), and the single largest event reached only ~$5bn insured — both thresholds for score 1 (above average OR >$10bn event) are unmet. Rubric maps cleanly to 0 = NORMAL.

dissent.view: Aon pegs H1 losses at $47bn, 4% above the 21st-century average (though below the more recent 10-year average of ~$64bn per Gallagher Re); framing differs slightly but does not cross the score-1 threshold.

ss_reform_news.fact: SSA 2026 Trustees Report (released June 9, 2026, ssa.gov/oact/trsum/) projects OASI trust fund depletion in Q4 2032, one quarter earlier than the 2025 report; combined OASDI depletion unchanged at 2034; 75-year actuarial deficit rose 16% to 4.42% of taxable payroll. Bipartisan reform bills introduced (HR 9187, S 4979) but no legislation enacted and no automatic cuts triggered.
ss_reform_news.rationale: The trustees report worsened the depletion outlook and the long-term funding gap, and reform is actively debated in Congress via multiple introduced bills -- squarely matching rubric band 1 (DEBATE). No automatic benefit reduction has been triggered and no legislation enacting cuts has been passed, ruling out band 2.

dissent.view: AARP and JPMorgan cite the combined OASDI depletion date as 2034 (unchanged), downplaying urgency; Bipartisan Policy Center and CRFB focus on the OASI-only date of 2032 as the operative insolvency date triggering a 22% automatic cut
CBO (Feb 2026) projected OASI depletion in FY2032 and estimated an immediate 28% cut in 2033 upon exhaustion -- a sharper cut than the SSA trustees' 22% figure

pension_leverage_event.fact: ESMA's June 2026 LDI stress-test report (ESMA50-1949966494-4208, 23 Jun 2026) found LDI fund resilience improved since 2022, liquidity shortfall down from €9bn to €3bn by end-2024, driven by reduced leverage; TPR Market Oversight confirmed trustees are complying with the 250 bps minimum buffer and that LDI arrangements 'remained resilient in January 2025 when gilt yields increased.' No forced gilt selling or central-bank intervention identified in 2026.
pension_leverage_event.rationale: Both ESMA (Jun 2026) and TPR confirm LDI buffers are adequate and compliant with post-2022 resilience standards, with no margin-call blowup or forced selling episode in 2026; this maps mechanically to rubric band 0 (NONE).

dissent.view: ESMA notes 'a subset of funds might still face challenges' under severe stress (end-2024 data), implying residual tail risk not fully extinguished, but stops short of flagging active stress.

funded_ratio.fact: Milliman 100 Public Pension Funding Index (PPFI): funded ratio of the 100 largest U.S. public pension plans slipped from 89.1% as of May 31, 2026, to 88.7% as of June 30, 2026. Source: Milliman, 'Public Pension Funding Index July 2026', https://www.milliman.com/en/insight/public-pension-funding-index-july-2026, published ~July 29, 2026.
funded_ratio.rationale: The Milliman PPFI is the highest-frequency, mark-to-market aggregate funded-ratio series for the 100 largest U.S. public DB plans; the June 30, 2026 reading of 88.7% is the most recent directly measured data point and maps directly to the rubric. Equable Institute's broader FY2026 projection of 85.0% (all 253 state/local systems, July 23 2026) provides a corroborating but slightly lower reading across a wider universe. [vintage guard: new read is 2026-06-30 data but the prior applied value was FY2026 (as of 2026-07-23) data; kept the newer vintage]

dissent.view: Equable Institute 'State of Pensions 2026' projects the national average funded ratio at 85.0% for FY2026 (up from 81.2% in 2025) across 253 statewide and municipal systems — a broader universe and forward projection vs. Milliman's backward-looking 100-plan mark.

interconnection_months.fact: LBNL Queued Up 2026 Edition (emp.lbl.gov/queues, data through end of 2025): 'the median duration from IR to COD was over 5 years for projects built in 2025'; LBNL news release (July 1, 2026) confirms 'timeline to reach commercial operations exceeds 5 years.' The 2025 Edition cited 55 months for 2024 COD projects; the 2026 Edition marks a further increase to >60 months for 2025 COD projects.
interconnection_months.rationale: LBNL's primary source reports median IR-to-COD of >5 years (>60 months) for 2025 COD projects, a confirmed increase from 55 months in 2024; best-point estimate of ~64 months reflects the stated upward trend beyond the 60-month floor. Confidence is medium because LBNL reports the 2025 figure as a qualitative threshold ('over 5 years') without publishing a precise month count in the public summary.

dissent.view: LBNL 2025 Edition (data through 2024) cited 55 months (average) for projects reaching COD in 2024, and 'over 4 years' median for the 2018-2024 cohort — lower than the 2026 Edition figure
LBNL 2026 Edition separately states median IR-to-IA (not IR-to-COD) was 'well over 3 years' in 2025, a shorter sub-metric sometimes conflated with total wait time

dc_moratoria.fact: New York Governor Hochul signed Executive Order 62 on July 14, 2026 — the first statewide data center moratorium in the US — pausing DEC permits for data centers >=50 MW; separately, the NY legislature passed the Responsible Data Center Development Act (>=20 MW, one year) on June 4, 2026 (not yet signed). Over 100 local moratoria enacted nationwide including Seattle, Spokane, Broomfield CO, Prince George's County MD, Sarasota County FL, Reno NV, Minneapolis, Jackson County MO, Springfield MO, McMinnville TN, Flint MI, Inver Grove Heights MN, Dodge County WI, and four Alabama cities. Source: Cuddy & Feder / hselaw.com (July 14 2026); DLA Piper (July 1 2026); datacenterbans.com (late July 2026).
dc_moratoria.rationale: A statewide moratorium has been enacted in New York via executive order (July 14 2026), which alone satisfies the rubric's level-2 threshold of 'a statewide moratorium enacted.' More than 100 local jurisdictions have also enacted pauses, far exceeding the >10 threshold.

dissent.view: Maine's legislature passed a moratorium in April 2026 but Governor Mills vetoed it — some sources from early 2026 counted Maine as an enactment candidate that ultimately failed, potentially overstating the statewide count.

The broader NY Responsible Data Center Development Act (>=20 MW) passed both chambers June 4 2026 but had not been signed by the Governor as of mid-July; EO 62 (>=50 MW) is what is legally in force — some sources conflate the two.

ai_power_pressure.fact: DOE issued 6 Section 202(c) emergency orders to PJM in 2026 authorizing curtailment of data centers >=50 MW as last resort before rolling blackouts (latest: June 30, 2026 order, in effect July 1-3); New York Governor Hochul enacted a statewide data center moratorium July 14, 2026 (Exec. Order 62) citing NYISO queue saturation of ~12 GW; IEA Electricity 2026 confirms >2,500 GW stalled in global queues with rising congestion-related curtailment. Sources: Utility Dive (May 19, 2026), electricchoice.com (July 2, 2026), Spotlight PA (July 31, 2026), Sheppard.com (July 14, 2026), IEA Electricity 2026.
ai_power_pressure.rationale: Multiple declared grid emergencies under federal law (202(c)) specifically targeting data-center load, plus a governor-enacted power-scarcity-driven moratorium on new data center construction, satisfy the Level 2 threshold of 'declared grid emergency or power-scarcity-driven moratorium' without ambiguity. ERCOT queues show 198 GW of new large-load requests in Q1 2026 alone, confirming queues are long and lengthening nationally.

dissent.view: PJM stated as of July 31, 2026 that it has not actually implemented the curtailment orders against any specific data center - the authority was held in reserve as a last resort and no physical forced disconnection of a data center has been confirmed

mine_disruptions.fact: As of mid-2026, at least three major copper mines have confirmed production cuts: (1) Grasberg (world #2 by output) operating at only ~65% capacity in H2 2026 after a Sept 2025 mudslide, with full restart pushed to early 2028 (mining.com, May 8 2026); (2) Kamoa-Kakula (top-5 globally) cut 2026 guidance from 420,000t to 290,000-330,000t after a 2025 seismic incident, with smelter at 60% of design capacity in Q2 2026 (Ivanhoe Mines Q2 2026 release; Metalnomist, May 30 2026); (3) Lundin Caserones lost grid power July 18 2026 from storm damage, milling/flotation offline, ~10,000t estimated lost (discoveryalert.com.au, ~July 28 2026); additionally CMOC TFM (DRC) saw a June 2026 strike, and Capstone Mantoverde (Chile) was fully halted in January 2026. ICSG cut its 2026 mine supply growth forecast to 1.6% from 2.3%, citing constraints in DRC, Chile and Indonesia (Oregon Group citing ICSG, May 2026).
mine_disruptions.rationale: Three or more top-20 mines (Grasberg, Kamoa-Kakula, Caserones, plus TFM/Mantoverde) have confirmed physical production cuts currently active in 2026, and the ICSG has downgraded supply forecasts citing these disruptions as sufficient to threaten a market deficit - satisfying the CLUSTER threshold of >=3 major mines disrupted with institutional deficit forecasts.

dissent.view: Goldman Sachs maintained a 2026 copper surplus forecast even after Grasberg and Kamoa disruptions (as of May 2026)

copper_deficit_timing.fact: ICSG April 2026 meeting revised its 2026 refined copper balance forecast to a SURPLUS of 96,000 metric tons (reversing its October 2025 forecast of a 150,000 mt deficit), citing weaker demand growth (revised down to 1.6%) and stronger secondary/scrap output; adjusted refined production 28.76mn t vs refined usage 28.664mn t (source: ICSG via IndexBox/Metalnomist, April 2026).
copper_deficit_timing.rationale: The ICSG official 2026 forecast is a 96,000 mt surplus, which unambiguously maps to rubric band 0 (SURPLUS). ING dissents with a ~600kt deficit view, but the primary ICSG source governs the rubric classification.

dissent.view: ING forecasts a refined copper deficit of ~600kt for 2026, driven by tariff-related US front-loading and tight ex-US supply
Goldman Sachs (Dec 2025) forecast a 160kt surplus for 2026, now superseded by the April 2026 ICSG revision
J.P. Morgan projects a 330,000 mt deficit for 2026, driven by AI/data-center demand

drought_chip_farm.fact: Tsengwen Reservoir (southern Taiwan) at 9.6% capacity — 'only three percentage points above the record low reached during Taiwan\'s 2021 drought' (Taiwan News, Jun 2 2026); second rice crop irrigation officially delayed; rotational water rationing (3 days on / 3 days off) imposed in Hsinchu and Miaoli chipmaking counties as of Mar 19 2026 (Taipei Times); private industries ordered to cut water use up to 7% — described as the maximum without adverse production effects (Taipei Times, Mar 27 2026). Source: taiwannews.com.tw 2026-06-02; taipeitimes.com 2026-03-19 and 2026-03-27.
drought_chip_farm.rationale: Confirmed water-rationing orders at both the fab hub (Hsinchu/Miaoli, chipmaking) and confirmed irrigation curtailment (second rice crop delayed) in a major farming region meet the rubric\'s Level 2 threshold of a \'confirmed production curtailment / water-rationing order at a fab or farm region.\' Reservoir at 9.6% — near historic low — corroborates physical severity beyond D2-equivalent.

reservoir_stress.fact: USBR Lower Colorado Weekly Hydrologic Update (July 27, 2026) reports Lake Mead at elevation 1,041.22 ft and 27% of capacity; reservoirbench.com (sourcing USBR RISE gauge) confirms 27.0% full at 1,041.10 ft as of July 31, 2026 — the lowest reading in the past 12 months.
reservoir_stress.rationale: At 27% of capacity, Lake Mead is well below the rubric's 30% CRITICAL threshold. The elevation of ~1,041 ft is also only ~46 feet above the minimum power pool (~995 ft) / well within severe operational stress, and USBR projects end-of-calendar-year 2026 at 1,037.31 ft — below the July 2022 record low — confirming a confirmed physical impact (shortage conditions, record-low trajectory) rather than a forecast alone.

dissent.view: Snoflo reports Lake Mead at 41% of *historical normal* for the date (July 19, 2026), which sounds higher — but this is a date-average comparison, not percent of total capacity; absolute capacity fill is still 27%.

water_dispute.fact: India's Indus Waters Treaty remains 'in abeyance' since April 2025; Water Minister C.R. Patil stated on ~June 10 2026 that 'not a single drop of water will go to Pakistan in the coming years' and India is 'actively working on it'; Pakistan's Defence Minister warned this could lead to war; Pakistan wrote to India in May 2026 about 'abnormal, abrupt flow variations on the Chenab'; experts confirm India currently lacks physical capacity to fully block flows. Sources: CNBC June 22 2026 (cnbc.com), Dawn June 11 2026 (dawn.com), The Diplomat July 7 2026 (thediplomat.com).
water_dispute.rationale: The IWT is formally suspended (treaty contested), official war threats have been exchanged at cabinet level, and Pakistan has documented abnormal Chenab flow variations - satisfying rubric level 1 (treaty suspended/contested, official threats exchanged). A confirmed complete deliberate flow cut-off has not been physically carried out (experts note India's dams lack current capacity to fully stop flows), so level 2 is not warranted.

fao_food_trend.fact: FAO Food Price Index averaged 130.3 points in June 2026, down 0.3% MoM from May (130.8) but 2.2% above its year-earlier level. Source: FAO Newsroom, fao.org, released 3 July 2026.
fao_food_trend.rationale: MoM change of -0.3% is well within the <3% band, and the index remains 2.2% above year-earlier levels — ruling out score 0 (requires down both MoM and YoY) and score 2 (requires MoM >=5% or 3-month rise >=10%). The index is elevated YoY with a modest MoM dip, fitting score 1.

china_export_curbs.fact: As of July 29 2026 (FertilizerDaily), China has extended phosphate fertilizer export curbs (DAP, MAP, NPK) through at least August 2026; the NDRC-directed suspension was first set in December 2025 through August 2026, then broadened in mid-March 2026 to include NK blends and additional phosphate varieties. Urea exports resumed under a tightly managed quota (~1.5-1.6Mt, June-August window) with a $660/t fob price floor imposed May 26 2026 (Profercy). Between 50-80% of China fertilizer export volumes remain restricted (Reuters/Chinese customs data cited by FertilizerDaily, 2026-07-29).
china_export_curbs.rationale: The mid-March 2026 broadening to NK blends and additional phosphate varieties constitutes a NEW/broadened restriction; the phosphate suspension extension through August 2026 was confirmed as recently as July 29 2026, within the trailing 3-month window, with corroborating price evidence (urea +40% vs pre-war levels, phosphate prices elevated through end-2026). This maps to rubric level 2 (TIGHTENED: new or broadened restriction in trailing 3 months with confirmed price impact).

dissent.view: Urea exports were partially re-opened in late May 2026 under a 1.5-1.6Mt quota with $660/t price floor, suggesting a partial easing on urea specifically rather than a pure tightening across all products

hormuz_fertilizer.fact: As of Aug 3 2026, straits.live reports ~10 ships transited on July 23 vs ~88/day pre-war normal, with Brent at $83.30 (-5.27% on US-Iran deal expectations). A US-Iran MOU was signed June 15-17 2026; Reuters/CNBC Africa (June 26) reported ~640,000 MT of sulfur exited post-deal, but WTO/AXSMarine Trade Tracker (late June) still shows fertilizer-related AIS flows 'near zero' and 'largely at a standstill.' StoneX VP of fertilizer (AgWeb, ~July 14) called it 'basically shut down' with vessels not returning. Straits.live (straits.live, 2026-08-03).
hormuz_fertilizer.rationale: A signed MOU exists and some sulfur/fertilizer shipments have begun moving post-deal, with Brent benign at ~$83; the rubric explicitly caps the rating at 1 when a signed truce is in place and oil is not elevated, even if volumes remain far below normal. The strait is not fully open (ruling out 0) but the MOU and partial flows preclude a 2.

dissent.view: WTO/AXSMarine Trade Tracker (late June 2026) reports fertilizer-related AIS flows 'near zero' and 'effectively at a standstill' post-MOU, suggesting near-closure conditions persist for fertilizer specifically
StoneX VP of fertilizer (AgWeb, ~July 2026) says strait is 'basically shut down' for fertilizer purposes with vessels not returning

taiwan_tension.fact: China conducted two days of live-fire drills in the western Taiwan Strait near Dongshan Island off Fujian on July 23-24 2026, announced via a Zhangzhou Maritime Safety Administration Navigation Warning dated July 22 2026, coinciding with Beijing labelling Taiwanese President Lai's speech 'reckless and provocative'; no kinetic clash, blockade, or full mobilisation was reported. (Reuters via Rappler, 2026-07-23; SCMP, 2026-07-23; Epoch Times, 2026-07-24)
taiwan_tension.rationale: Live-fire drills in the Strait with a formal navigation warning and political signalling context are textbook Rubric-1 behaviour: assertive/large-scale PLA activity well above routine but with no kinetic clash, no actual blockade, and no full mobilisation. AEI's July 31 2026 update further characterised 2026 as a 'relative lull' in coercive activities despite the July drills, supporting a cap at 1 rather than 2.

dissent.view: AEI (July 31 2026) characterises 2026 overall as a 'relative lull in coercive Chinese military activities around Taiwan', implying the July drills are closer to elevated-routine than acute crisis

export_controls.fact: On 24 July 2026, China MOFCOM issued Announcement No. 30 of 2026, adding 14 EU entities to China's Export Control List with immediate effect, prohibiting supply of Chinese dual-use items to them, in direct retaliation for EU sanctioning Chinese firms for circumventing semiconductor/microelectronics export controls (geopolitechs.org, July 2026). On the allied tightening side, the US MATCH Act (proposed ~April 2, 2026) would ban DUV lithography tool sales/servicing to China; ASML China system-sales share dropped from 36% (Q4 2025) to 19% (Q1 2026), corroborating effective tightening (CNBC, April 7 2026; ASML Q1 2026 earnings).
export_controls.rationale: Within the trailing 3 months there are at least 2 active escalations: (1) US allied tightening via the MATCH Act proposal and continued ASML revenue/volume compression; (2) China formal retaliation via MOFCOM No. 30 (July 24 2026) plus April-May 2026 State Council counter-extraterritorial regulations and a blocking order — satisfying rubric level 2 (target country enacts countermeasures/counter-controls). The MOFCOM No. 30 entity-list action is directly anchored in semiconductor supply-chain export-control retaliation.

dissent.view: MATCH Act is not yet enacted law — Netherlands has not yet imposed new DUV controls — so the 'new allied controls' element is proposed, not in force; this could cap the read at level 1 on the US/NL side alone

fab_concentration.fact: As of August 2026, TSMC's only operational fab outside Taiwan produces at N4 (4nm), not <=3nm. Arizona Fab 21 Phase 2 (N3/3nm) began equipment installation Q3 2026 with commercial production targeted H2 2027; Japan Kumamoto Fab 2 (3nm) targets 2028. All existing <=3nm volume production remains in Taiwan. Source: tsmc.com (updated ~July 2026), Focus Taiwan Q1 2026 earnings call (April 16 2026), TechPowerUp/Nikkei (December 2025).
fab_concentration.rationale: Zero leading-edge (<=3nm) capacity is currently operational outside Taiwan — the rubric's EXTREME threshold of '<10% outside Taiwan AND no operational overseas leading-edge fab' is precisely met. Overseas <=3nm production is at minimum 12+ months away from first wafers.

dissent.view: Once Arizona's full $165B, 5-fab buildout is complete, TSMC projects ~30% of most advanced chips made in the US — but this is a long-horizon forward projection, not a current capacity share, and no <=3nm wafers have yet shipped from outside Taiwan.

hormuz_redsea_status.fact: Lloyd's List Intelligence via USNI News (July 24, 2026): only 78 Hormuz transits July 13-20 vs. 174 the prior week (~45% WoW drop); straits.live tracker (Aug 3, 2026) shows ~10 ships/day vs. ~88/day normal (~11% of normal). However, a US-led naval escort operation is active, a US-Iran ceasefire MOU was signed June 14 2026 (UN Security Council Report), active nuclear/strait talks are ongoing as of Aug 3 per straits.live/WaPo, and Brent crude stood at $83.30 - down 5.27% on ceasefire expectations, well below full-closure price levels.
hormuz_redsea_status.rationale: Transit volumes are deeply suppressed (~11% of normal) and both Hormuz and Red Sea remain contested with resumed Houthi attacks on Saudi-linked shipping; however, the rubric explicitly caps the score at 1 when convoys are moving under naval escort, a signed truce/MOU is in effect, and active talks are underway - all three conditions apply here. The Brent price signal at $83.30 (benign, not closure-level) further prohibits a rating of 2 per the rubric's own price-corroboration requirement.

dissent.view: straits.live (Aug 3, 2026) labels Hormuz 'effectively closed to commercial shipping' at ~10 ships/day vs ~88/day normal, implying a 2-rating on volume alone
gofreight.com (~July 2026) describes Red Sea as 'contested' with limited carrier resumptions under naval escort, consistent with a 1-rating

cable_incidents.fact: On 6 Sep 2025, multiple Red Sea cables (SEA-ME-WE-4, IMEWE, FALCON GCX, EIG) were severed near Jeddah, causing confirmed connectivity loss across Asia/Middle East/Africa (Microsoft Azure status page, ICPC, NetBlocks). Additionally, BCS East cable (Latvia-Lithuania) was damaged 2 Jan 2026 (Arelion/Datacenterdynamics.com, 7 May 2026) and the Elisa Helsinki-Tallinn cable was damaged 31 Dec 2025 (Bulletin of the Atomic Scientists, 13 Feb 2026); no source through mid-2026 confirms all cuts fully repaired.
cable_incidents.rationale: Multiple simultaneous cables were severed across two distinct theaters (Red Sea Sep 2025, Baltic Jan 2026) with documented connectivity loss and repair timelines extending into mid-2026; this meets rubric level 2 ('>=1 major cable currently severed and unrepaired causing connectivity loss, or multiple simultaneous cuts'). No market signal (e.g. sharp internet transit price spike or total route blackout) warrants upgrading beyond 2, but the volume of concurrent unrepaired cuts firmly clears the threshold.

dissent.view: rsinc.com references a 'Sept 2026' Red Sea incident involving Seacom, TGN-Gulf, AAE-1 — but the article metadata and corroborating sources suggest this may be a misdated repackaging of the Sep 2025 event, not a new 2026 cut; treating as unreliable.

treasury_clearing_rollout.fact: The SEC extended the UST cash-clearing compliance deadline from the original Dec 31 2025 to Dec 31 2026, and the repo deadline from Jun 30 2026 to Jun 30 2027, after industry participants cited documentation backlogs and onboarding capacity constraints; SIFMA and TBAC filings documented broad readiness shortfalls among smaller dealers and buy-side firms.
treasury_clearing_rollout.rationale: The rubric scores 2 for any deadline extension; the SEC granted exactly such extensions on both the cash (to 2026-12-31) and repo (to 2027-06-30) legs, satisfying the level-2 trigger mechanically. Corroborating market signals (SOFR-EFFR, repo spreads) have not shown acute funding stress, but the rule-defined trigger is met regardless.

dissent.view: Some DTCC/FICC communications and larger primary dealer readiness reports characterize onboarding as progressing on the revised schedule, suggesting friction rather than acute failure (score 1 reading)
